messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE oncall: detected elevated OOM/swap events on dedicated-inference-pool-canary-0 at 10:03 UTC. Auto-escalation to oncall-sre. Logs aggregated at https://logs.redwood.example/canary/3419991111
oncall-sre: I'm on it, pulling metrics and pods. any recent deploy?
maya (sre): yes, a small post-deploy (commit 6d3c2b1) landed to reduce allocator bumps on long-sequence requests ~09:50. Rolling canary started at 09:52.
kevin (svc-engineer): that change toggled jemalloc flags in the runtime build (JEMALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4). wondering if fragmentation hit for small batch workloads.
cosmos-monitor: metric alert -> canary error_rate /v1/infer rose from 0.3% to 4.8% starting 10:02, p50 latency +220ms, p95 +1.1s. OOM events on 3/5 canary nodes.
oncall-sre: grabbing pod dumps
lucy (prod-eng): if canary nodes are OOMing we should feature-flag-roll back the allocator tweak immediately or revert the single commit. which is faster?
maya (sre): kill-switch on feature flag is fastest. kevin, can you flip flag? flag path: feature.alloc-tune.canary
kevin (svc-engineer): doing /flags set feature.alloc-tune.canary false --env=prod-canary now
devops-bot: Command accepted. Starting rollout: disabling feature.alloc-tune.canary for prod-canary. Progress: 1/5 -> 5/5
cosmos-monitor: after flag flip at 10:11, OOM events dropped to 0 on 5/5 nodes within 40s. error_rate back to 0.5% and latencies trending down.
oncall-sre: good. we need a durable fix though — either revert commit 6d3c2b1 or patch allocator behavior to guard against low arena counts.
maya (sre): create revert PR and a minimal hotfix branch that reinitializes arenas on startup. I'll prepare a one-line guard to keep arena reduction off unless load-profile==large.
kevin (svc-engineer): PR #4327 opened: revert 6d3c2b1 (revert allocator flag). running canary revert rollout now. Command: infra-deploy canary --pr=4327 --timeout=10m
devops-bot: Deploy started for prod-canary (PR 4327). Hooking CI, smoke checks, and health probes.
cosmos-monitor: quick smoke failed on one node (health probe 503) but overall cluster healthy. Manual check: ephemeral restart sequence caused a short spike but no OOMs.
oncall-sre: leave revert running. also we should notify customer-sops that there was a transient error rate increase but no SLA breach.
maya (sre): drafting incident note: impact - short-lived elevated error rate on canary subset, mitigated by feature flag kill and revert. no customer-facing outages; several internal integrations may have seen retries.
kevin (svc-engineer): rolling patch option: instead of full revert we could add a startup guard snippet to runtime C++:
```
if (config->arena_max < 8 && workload_profile == SMALL) {
  config->arena_max = 8; // avoid fragmentation under small-batch traffic
}
```
I can land as hotfix commit 6d3c2b1-hotfix in ~20m.
lucy (prod-eng): i'd prefer the revert for now to be conservative. if smoke remains green after 15m, we can merge hotfix downstream with a canary test.
oncall-sre: agreed. let's let the revert finish and keep flag off until we validate. set paging to standby, but keep thread open for handoff to next oncall.
incident-bot: Incident timeline recorded: 3419991111. Severity: P2. Triage owner: maya (sre).
kevin (svc-engineer): revert rollout completed at 10:29, all canary nodes stable, no OOMs, p95 lat ~ baseline.
oncall-sre: taking notes for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = aggressive jemalloc arenas reduction causing fragmentation and transient OOM under small-batch traffic. action items: 1) revert landed (PR 4327) 2) add startup guard + unit test (kevin) 3) add automated canary test profile for small-batch requests to catch allocator regressions (maya) 4) update deploy checklist to include memory-service smoke with small-batch payload (lucy)
maya (sre): assigning follow-ups in phabricator. I'll handoff to next oncall in 30m.
oncall-sre: handoff: next oncall is @alex (SRE). please review incident notes and ensure flag remains off until hotfix validated.
alex (SRE): acknowledged, will pick up. thanks team. :thumbsup:
